idiom_name: JPA entities in Kotlin via the kotlin-jpa no-arg plugin
implementation_notes: In Kotlin the composite entity is a JPA entity with @OneToMany dependents or @Embeddable components exactly as in Java; what changes is the language integration, because Kotlin classes have no implicit no-argument constructor and JPA requires one. The kotlin-jpa compiler plugin (wrapped on top of no-arg) generates the synthetic no-arg constructor for @Entity, @Embeddable and @MappedSuperclass, which is what makes primary-constructor classes usable as entities at all. Keep declarative mapping on the class and let the persistence context flush the graph; use immutable data classes for embeddable value components, not for entities, which must stay mutable and proxyable.
pitfalls: Without the kotlin-jpa plugin Hibernate fails at runtime with a missing default constructor even though the code compiles.
val collections, data-class equals/hashCode and generated ids are a poor fit for entities: Hibernate proxies and lazy loading break both invariants.
Entity classes also need the all-open plugin for proxy generation, otherwise lazy relationships cannot be instrumented.
